activity_modelled: Scaled from another body's record rather than measured on this one.
activity_upper_limit: An upper limit from a non-detection, not a measurement.
structure_layer_derived: The mass is calculated from the source's radii and densities rather than quoted by it.
structure_layer_no_boundaries: No internal boundaries have been resolved; the composition changes continuously with depth.
zone_def_IEO: Atira — orbit entirely inside Earth's (Q < 0.983 AU).
zone_def_ATE: Aten — Earth-crossing, smaller than Earth's (a < 1.0 AU, Q > 0.983 AU).
zone_def_APO: Apollo — Earth-crossing, larger than Earth's (a > 1.0 AU, q < 1.017 AU).
zone_def_AMO: Amor — approaches Earth from outside (1.017 < q < 1.3 AU).
zone_def_IMB: Inner main belt — 1.666 < q AU and a < 2.0 AU.
zone_def_MBA: Main belt — between Mars and Jupiter (2.0 < a < 3.2 AU, q > 1.666 AU).
zone_def_TJN: Jupiter Trojan — locked in 1:1 resonance at Jupiter's L4/L5 (a ≈ 5.2 AU, e < 0.3).
zone_def_CEN: Centaur — between the giant planets (5.5 < a < 30.1 AU).
zone_def_JFC: Jupiter-family comet (classical) — orbital period under 20 years.
zone_def_HTC: Halley-type comet — T_J < 2, period under 200 years.
zone_def_ETc: Encke-type comet — T_J > 3 with a < Jupiter's; very short period.
zone_def_CTc: Chiron-type comet — T_J > 3 with a > Jupiter's; Centaur-like.
zone_def_PAR: Parabolic comet — eccentricity = 1; orbit is just barely bound.
zone_def_PAA: Parabolic asteroid — eccentricity = 1; asteroid-designated, barely bound.
zone_def_HYP: Hyperbolic comet — eccentricity > 1; escaping the solar system.
zone_def_HYA: Hyperbolic asteroid — eccentricity > 1; escape trajectory (interstellar candidate).
zone_def_AST: Asteroid — matches no other class; near Jupiter but too eccentric for the Trojans (4.6 < a < 5.5 AU, e > 0.3).
zone_def_COM: Comet — orbit doesn't match any specific family.
zone_def_VLEO: Very Low Earth Orbit — apogee under 600 km; most active sats live here despite high drag.
zone_def_MEO: Medium Earth Orbit — between LEO and the synchronous band; eccentricity under 0.5.
zone_def_GSO: Geosynchronous — near the synchronous band (±2000 km of 35786 km); not matching a more specific sync class.
zone_def_HEO: Highly elliptical Earth orbit — eccentricity 0.5 or more with apogee up to 50000 km; not matching a more specific class.
zone_def_CIS: Cislunar — apogee between 50000 km and the Moon's distance (~400000 km); perigee below the synchronous band.
zone_def_VHEO: Very high Earth orbit — apogee beyond the Moon (over 500000 km).
zone_def_GTO: Geostationary Transfer Orbit — low perigee with apogee near GEO; used to lift sats to GEO (Molniya inclinations excluded).
zone_def_GEO: Geostationary — GSO with inclination under 3° (fixed point above the equator).
zone_def_IGSO: Inclined geosynchronous — GSO with inclination above 3°; ground track traces a figure eight.
zone_def_GRA: Graveyard — disposal band starting ~200 km above GEO where retired GEO sats are parked.
zone_def_HIGH: High Earth orbit — entirely above the synchronous band; apogee under 500000 km.
zone_def_MOL: Molniya — HEO with apogee near GEO and inclination 62–64°; ~12-hour period.
zone_def_TUN: Tundra — eccentric geosynchronous with 63.4° inclination; ~24-hour period.
zone_def_SSO: Sun-synchronous — LEO with inclination 95–104°; orbit precesses with the Sun.
zone_def_POL: Polar — inclination 85–95°; sat passes over both poles.
zone_def_RET: Retrograde — inclination above 104°; orbits opposite Earth's spin.
zone_def_EQU: Equatorial — inclination under 25°; stays close to the equatorial plane.
zone_def_EL1: Sun–Earth L1 — libration point ~1.5 million km sunward of Earth; spacecraft orbit the Sun, station-kept at L1.
zone_def_EL2: Sun–Earth L2 — libration point ~1.5 million km anti-sunward of Earth; spacecraft orbit the Sun, station-kept at L2.

atmosphere_note_photosphere: Quoted at the photosphere, the depth at which the Sun becomes opaque. A star has no surface, only gas that thins outwards.
atmosphere_note_surface_bounded: Surface-bounded exosphere: atoms released from the surface by sunlight, solar wind and micrometeorite impacts, so sparse that they rarely collide with one another.
atmosphere_note_sputtered_ice: Sputtered from the ice: charged particles trapped in the planet's magnetic field chip molecules off the surface faster than they escape.
atmosphere_note_volcanic: Fed by Io's volcanoes and by sulphur dioxide subliming from surface frost. Most of it condenses back onto the surface during the two hours each orbit that Io spends in Jupiter's shadow, and returns when it emerges.
atmosphere_note_seasonal_cap: Seasonal: roughly a quarter of the air freezes onto the winter polar cap and returns half a year later.
atmosphere_note_seasonal_orbit: Seasonal along the orbit: nitrogen frost sublimates as the body nears the Sun and freezes back out as it recedes, so the pressure quoted is one moment in a decades-long cycle.
atmosphere_note_frozen_out: Far enough out that any atmosphere has frozen onto the surface; it should return near perihelion.
atmosphere_note_no_detection: No global atmosphere: during stellar occultations the starlight dims too abruptly for one, which sets the upper limit above.
atmosphere_note_plume: Not a global atmosphere: a plume of water vapour venting from fractures at the south pole, feeding Saturn's E ring.
atmosphere_note_transient_vapour: Intermittent: water vapour appears where sunlight reaches surface ice, and is not always present.
atmosphere_composition_relative_density: Shares of the measured column and number densities rather than a mixing ratio. The gases were measured separately, and some values are upper limits.
atmosphere_composition_by_mass: Shares by mass, not by number of particles.

tooltip_longitude: Longitude on the parent body directly below the object (positive = east)

tooltip_temperature_estimated: No measurement exists for this body. The value is its radiative equilibrium temperature, calculated from its distance from the Sun and its albedo.
tooltip_temperature_scale: Position on a fixed scale from absolute zero to 1000 K. The green band marks where water is liquid at 1 atm.
tooltip_temperature_scale_stellar: Position on a logarithmic scale from 1000 K to 100 million K, tinted with the colour a blackbody glows at that temperature.
interior_note_subsurface_ocean: A layer of liquid water lies beneath the outer shell.
interior_note_rubble_pile: A loose aggregate of debris held together by gravity rather than a single solid body.
structure_layer_diffuse: It has no sharp boundary and fades into the layer above.
structure_interior_chart: Cross-section through the body, showing {count} layers
structure_atmosphere_chart: Cross-section through the atmosphere, showing its named layers
structure_atmosphere_scale: Drawn to scale up to {top} above the {datum}.
structure_atmosphere_scale_height: The atmosphere has no measured boundaries. Its density falls by a factor of about 2.7 every {value}.
structure_atmosphere_homopause: The gases stay mixed up to {value}. Above that they separate by weight.
atmosphere_structure_note_well_mixed: The gases stay mixed here, so this layer has the same composition as the atmosphere as a whole.
atmosphere_structure_note_heterosphere: The gases separate by weight above this height, so no single mixture describes the layer.
atmosphere_structure_note_no_inversion: A carbon dioxide atmosphere absorbs little sunlight at these heights, so no warm layer forms above this one.
atmosphere_structure_note_nightside_cryo: On the night side this layer cools enough for its gases to freeze onto the surface.
atmosphere_structure_note_seasonal_dust: Dust storms lift this layer and warm it through the year.
atmosphere_structure_note_weakly_defined: The literature names this layer, but the measurements barely separate it from the ones around it.
atmosphere_structure_note_diffuse_top: The layer fades out with height rather than ending at a boundary.
atmosphere_structure_note_haze_layers: Photochemical haze forms in detached layers through this region.
atmosphere_structure_note_exobase: Above this height a molecule is more likely to escape than to hit another one.
interior_note_taxonomy_estimate: Composition inferred by matching the body's reflectance spectrum to meteorite types.

feature_type_description_crater: Circular depression in a solid astronomical body formed by the impact of a smaller object

feature_type_description_flexus: Very low curvilinear ridge with a scalloped pattern
feature_type_description_fluctus: Terrain covered by outflow of liquid on Venus, Io or Titan
feature_type_description_flumen: Channel on Titan that might carry liquid
feature_type_description_fretum: Strait of liquid connecting two larger areas of liquid on Titan
feature_type_description_insula: Isolated land area surrounded by a liquid area on Titan
feature_type_description_labes: Landslide, especially on Mars' Valles Marineris

feature_type_description_lacuna: Irregularly shaped depression having the appearance of a dry lake bed on Titan
feature_type_description_lacus: Small plain on the Moon or Mars; small, dark plain with discrete, sharp boundaries on Titan
feature_type_description_lingula: Extension of plateau having rounded lobate or tongue-like boundaries on Mars
feature_type_description_lobus: One of two lobes of a contact binary asteroid
feature_type_description_macula: Unusually dark area on the surface of a planet or moon
feature_type_description_mare: Large circular plain on the Moon and Mars; large expanses of dark materials thought to be liquid hydrocarbons on Titan
feature_type_description_palus: Small plain on the Moon or Mars
feature_type_description_planum: Plateau or high plain on other planets
feature_type_description_regio: Large area marked by reflectivity or color distinctions from adjacent areas
feature_type_description_satellite-featu: Feature that shares the name of an associated feature
feature_type_description_saxum: Rock on an astronomical body of scientific importance and measuring at least 1% of the diameter of the parent body
feature_type_description_serpens: Sinuous feature with segments of positive and negative relief along its length
feature_type_description_sinus: Small plain on the Moon or Mars
feature_type_description_sulcus: Area of complex parallel or subparallel ridges and furrows on an astronomical object
feature_type_description_terra: Extensive land mass on a celestial body
feature_type_description_tessera: Area of tile-like, polygonal terrain on Venus
feature_type_description_unda: Field of dunes on Venus, Mars or Titan
feature_type_description_virga: Streak or stripe of color on Titan
